content.intro: This lesson covers Macro Matching and Repetition. It sits in Module 19, Macros and Metaprogramming, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Macro Matching and Repetition matters when you work with data modelling and exhaustive handling. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Macros transform token streams before or during compilation, allowing patterns that ordinary functions cannot express. Prefer ordinary functions when they are sufficient, and test macro expansions as public API.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Macro Matching and Repetition, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not assume Macro Matching and Repetition guarantees more than it actually does. Reduce a failure to a small reproducer, read the full compiler diagnostic or error value, consult the matching official reference, and change one assumption at a time.
